problem_statement:
csv2rdf uses Python 2 features broken by Python 3
I have tried to run **csv2rdf** under both Windows 10 and a(n Alpine) Linux Docker container and it failed both times, due to differences between Python 2 and Python 3 strings and bytestreams.

I have been able to patch the module using the following three **sed** commands:

```sh
# Replace .next() with next(...)
sed -i 's/header_labels = list(csvreader.next())/header_labels = list(next(csvreader))/g' /usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/rdflib/tools/csv2rdf.py

# Python 3 strings are natively Unicode
sed -i 's/yield \[str(cell, "utf-8", errors="replace") for cell in row\]/yield \[cell for cell in row\]/g' /usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/rdflib/tools/csv2rdf.py

# Reference https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4374455/how-to-set-sys-stdout-encoding-in-python-3
sed -i 's/self.OUT = codecs.getwriter("utf-8")(sys.stdout, errors="replace")/self.OUT = codecs.getwriter("utf-8")(sys.stdout.detach(), errors="replace")/g' /usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/rdflib/tools/csv2rdf.py
```

but this seems to alter some of **csv2rdf**'s incidental behaviour, such as showing the help text and printing extra output about the buffer being detatched.

It would be good if someone who knew what they were doing could take a look at this and update this tool for Python 3.
